newsitem.title: UK: European veg oils slip into holiday mode.
newsitem.headline: European veg oils slip into holiday mode.

text.p: European soft oil sellers on Thursday took their cue from the higher overnight close in Chicago but traders said the market seems to be slipping into holiday mode.
Apart from the higher Chicago values traders said there appeared to be little else to go on.
"We are still trying to find some kind of lead to hang the market on today," one said.
Palm oil was unchanged despite the lower close in Malaysia.
Traders said the market appeared to be slipping into the doldrums ahead of Christmas and New Year.
"It seems a bit early but unless something unexpected happens all the factors are known up to the end of the year," said a trader.
Traders said there was a possibility of one or two small tenders for palm oil from Pakistan between now and the end of the year, but at current levels India was unlikely to be seen.

Corncern over genetically-altered soybeans remains a background feature and along with tight supplies of rape seed to the crushers is keeping rape oil's premium over soy oil at around 3.50 to five guilders.
Despite volatile currencies and concern over freight space prices on Thursday were little changed from the same day last week.
Dutch soy oil opened with January at 89.50 guilders against 90 guilders, 0.50 down while rape oil opened at 94 against 94.50 guilders also 0.50 guilders lower.
December crude palm oil opened at $580 against $572.50, $7.50 up mainly due to tightness in nearby supplies while Apr/Jun sellers were at $542.50 against $550, $7.50 down.
Coconut oil prices have been fairly stable over the past week with Nov/Dec offered at $810 at the opening against $815 last week.
At the opening on Thursday Dutch soy oil was 0.50 guilders up to unchanged and rape oil 0.25 to 0.50 guilders up.
Based on sellers' prices, the premium for rape oil over soyoil was four to 4.50 guilders at the opening against 3.75 to 4.50 guilders at Wednesday's close.
Crude palm oil sellers were unchanged to $2.50 down in a so far tradeless market.
Coconut oil started the day $5 up while palmkernel oil was not quoted.
